steps: Choose the triangle: speed (D, S, T), density (M, D, V) or pressure (F, P, A).
Cover the quantity you want: it shows you whether to multiply or divide.
Match the units first (convert if needed), then calculate and add the units.
method_card.title: Speed, Density & Pressure
method_card.content:
Speed: \(S = \frac{D}{T}\), Distance = Speed × Time, Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

Density: \(D = \frac{M}{V}\), Mass = Density × Volume.

Pressure: \(P = \frac{F}{A}\), Force = Pressure × Area.
method_card.example:
A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. Speed?

S = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 mph.

bronze.display: A car travels 180 km in 3 hours. What is the speed in km/h?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time, so divide: 180 ÷ 3 = 60. Multiplying gives 540, far too fast for a car.

guided_steps.say: Speed = distance ÷ time. The distance is 180 km and the time is 3 hours.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
Share the distance equally over the 3 hours.

guided_steps.done: Back to 180, so 60 km/h is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 180 km, something slipped.

bronze.display: A cyclist travels at 12 km/h for 3 hours. How far do they go?

misconceptions.message: To find distance, multiply: 12 × 3 = 36 km. Dividing gives 4, which is smaller than one hour's travel.

guided_steps.say: Distance = speed × time. The speed is 12 km/h and the time is 3 hours.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you multiply by.
Three hours at 12 km each hour.

guided_steps.done: Back to 12, so 36 km is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 12 km/h, something slipped.

bronze.display: A runner covers 400 m in 80 seconds. What is their speed in m/s?

misconceptions.message: Divide distance by time, not time by distance: 400 ÷ 80 = 5 m/s. 80 ÷ 400 gives 0.2, the wrong way round.

guided_steps.say: Speed = distance ÷ time. The distance is 400 m and the time is 80 s.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
How many metres in one second?

guided_steps.done: Back to 400, so 5 m/s is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 400 m, something slipped.

bronze.display: An object has mass 60 g and volume 20 cm³. Find the density.

misconceptions.message: Density = mass ÷ volume, so divide: 60 ÷ 20 = 3 g/cm³. Multiplying gives 1200, which is not a density.

guided_steps.say: Density = mass ÷ volume. The mass is 60 g and the volume is 20 cm³.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
How much mass sits in each cm³?

guided_steps.done: Back to 60, so 3 g/cm³ is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 60 g, something slipped.

bronze.display: Density = 5 g/cm³, Volume = 8 cm³. Find the mass.

misconceptions.message: Mass = density × volume, so multiply: 5 × 8 = 40 g. Dividing gives 1.6, too light for 8 cm³.

guided_steps.say: Mass = density × volume. The density is 5 g/cm³ and the volume is 8 cm³.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you multiply by.
Eight lots of 5 g.

guided_steps.done: Back to 5, so 40 g is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 5 g/cm³, something slipped.

bronze.display: A train travels at 80 mph for 2.5 hours. How far does it go?

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time, so multiply: 80 × 2.5 = 200 miles. Dividing gives 32, less than one hour's travel.

guided_steps.say: Distance = speed × time. The speed is 80 mph and the time is 2.5 hours.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you multiply by.
Eighty miles for each of the 2.5 hours.

guided_steps.done: Back to 80, so 200 miles is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 80 mph, something slipped.

bronze.display: Mass = 150 g, Density = 6 g/cm³. Find the volume.

misconceptions.message: Volume = mass ÷ density, so divide: 150 ÷ 6 = 25 cm³. Multiplying gives 900, far too large.

guided_steps.say: Volume = mass ÷ density. The mass is 150 g and the density is 6 g/cm³.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
How many cm³ does 150 g fill at 6 g each?

guided_steps.done: Back to 150, so 25 cm³ is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 150 g, something slipped.

bronze.display: A journey of 84 miles takes 1.5 hours. What is the speed?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time, so divide: 84 ÷ 1.5 = 56 mph. Multiplying gives 126, faster than any leg of the trip.

guided_steps.say: Speed = distance ÷ time. The distance is 84 miles and the time is 1.5 hours.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
Double both to make it easy: 168 ÷ 3.

guided_steps.done: Back to 84, so 56 mph is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 84 miles, something slipped.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One formula used once: divide (or multiply) the two numbers given and write the units.

silver.display: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 4 m². Find the pressure in N/m².

misconceptions.message: Pressure = force ÷ area, so divide: 200 ÷ 4 = 50 N/m². Multiplying gives 800.

guided_steps.say: Pressure = force ÷ area. Cover P in the triangle to see the divide. Force is 200 N, area is 4 m².

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
Spread the 200 N over the 4 m².

guided_steps.done: Back to 200, so 50 N/m² is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 200 N, something slipped.

silver.display: Pressure = 500 Pa, Area = 0.3 m². Find the force.

misconceptions.message: The area is 0.3 m², not 3. Force = 500 × 0.3 = 150 N. Using 3 gives 1500 N, ten times too big.

guided_steps.say: Force is the top of the pressure triangle: F = pressure × area.

guided_steps.pre: Read the area as a decimal: 0.3 m², so multiply 500 ×
guided_steps.hint: It is 0.3, not 3.
Half of 300 is 150.

guided_steps.done: Back to 500 Pa, so 150 N is right.
guided_steps.hint: Dividing undoes the multiply.

silver.display: A car travels 30 km at 60 km/h then 40 km at 80 km/h. Find the total time in hours. Give as a decimal.
silver.hint: Find each leg's time separately, then add them.

misconceptions.message: Add the two times, do not divide total distance by total speed. 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 h and 40 ÷ 80 = 0.5 h, total 1 hour. (30+40) ÷ (60+80) gives 0.5, which is wrong.

guided_steps.say: Total time = time for leg 1 + time for leg 2. Each time = distance ÷ speed.

guided_steps.hint: Thirty km at 60 km/h is half an hour.
Forty km at 80 km/h is half an hour.
Add the two half hours.

guided_steps.done: Back to 30 km, so the times are right.
guided_steps.hint: Speed times time gives the distance.

silver.hint: To go from km/h to m/s, divide by 3.6.

misconceptions.message: km/h to m/s divides by 3.6: 72 ÷ 3.6 = 20 m/s. Multiplying by 3.6 gives 259.2, which is faster than sound.

guided_steps.say: km/h to m/s: divide by 3.6 (there are 3.6 km/h in each 1 m/s).

guided_steps.hint: It is the number given in the question.

guided_steps.done: Back to 72 km/h, so 20 m/s is right.
guided_steps.hint: Multiplying by 3.6 undoes the divide.

silver.display: An alloy has density 7.5 g/cm³ and mass 225 g. Find the volume.

misconceptions.message: Volume = mass ÷ density, so divide: 225 ÷ 7.5 = 30 cm³. Multiplying gives 1687.5.

guided_steps.say: Volume = mass ÷ density. Cover V in the triangle. Mass is 225 g, density is 7.5 g/cm³.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
How many cm³ at 7.5 g each make 225 g?

guided_steps.done: Back to 225, so 30 cm³ is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 225 g, something slipped.

silver.display: Force = 800 N, Pressure = 400 Pa. Find the area.

misconceptions.message: Area = force ÷ pressure, so divide: 800 ÷ 400 = 2 m². Multiplying gives 320000.

guided_steps.say: Area = force ÷ pressure. Cover A in the triangle. Force is 800 N, pressure is 400 Pa.

guided_steps.hint: This is the number you divide by.
How many m² at 400 Pa each carry 800 N?

guided_steps.done: Back to 800, so 2 m² is right.
guided_steps.hint: If it does not give back 800 N, something slipped.

silver.display: A journey takes 45 minutes at 80 km/h. How far in km?
silver.hint: Turn 45 minutes into hours first, then multiply by the speed.

misconceptions.message: 45 minutes = 0.75 hours, not 45. Distance = 80 × 0.75 = 60 km. Using 45 gives 3600 km.

guided_steps.say: Distance = speed × time, but time must be in hours. 45 minutes = 45 ÷ 60 hours.

guided_steps.hint: 45 out of 60 minutes is three quarters.
Three quarters of 80.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.75 hours, so 60 km is right.
guided_steps.hint: Distance ÷ speed gives the time.

problem_bank.silver_description: Rearrange the triangle or convert a unit first, then apply the formula in one step.

gold.display: A car travels 60 km at 40 km/h, then 60 km at 60 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey in km/h. Give to 1 d.p.
gold.hint: Average speed = total distance divided by total time. Find each time first.

misconceptions.message: The average of 40 and 60 is 50, but more time is spent at the slower speed. Use total distance ÷ total time = 120 ÷ 2.5 = 48 km/h.

guided_steps.say: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Find each leg's time first.

guided_steps.hint: Distance ÷ speed.
Distance ÷ speed.
Add the two distances.
Add the two times.
Total distance ÷ total time.

guided_steps.done: Back to the total distance, so 48 km/h is right.
guided_steps.hint: Average speed times total time gives total distance.

gold.display: A cube has side 4 cm and mass 384 g. Find the density.Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: Find the volume of the cube first, then divide the mass by it.

misconceptions.message: The volume of a cube is side³ = 4³ = 64, not 4² = 16. Density = 384 ÷ 64 = 6 g/cm³. Using 16 gives 24.

guided_steps.say: Density = mass ÷ volume. First the volume of the cube: side × side × side.

guided_steps.hint: Cube the side: 4³.
Mass ÷ volume.

guided_steps.done: Back to the mass, so 6 g/cm³ is right.
guided_steps.hint: Density times volume gives the mass.

gold.display: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm and mass 848 g. Find the density to 1 d.p.Diagram not drawn accurately
gold.hint: Volume of a cylinder is pi times radius squared times height.

misconceptions.message: Volume = πr²h and r² = 9, so V ≈ 282.7 cm³ and density ≈ 848 ÷ 282.7 ≈ 3.0. Using r instead of r² gives about 9.

guided_steps.say: Density = mass ÷ volume. Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h. Use π ≈ 3.142.

guided_steps.hint: r² comes before multiplying by π.
Mass ÷ volume, rounded to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.done: Back to the volume, so 3.0 g/cm³ is right.
guided_steps.hint: Mass ÷ density returns the volume.

gold.display: A woman of mass 55 kg stands on one heel of area 2 cm² = 0.0002 m². Find the pressure in Pa. (Use g = 10.)
gold.hint: Turn her mass into a force (weight = mass times g) before dividing by the area.

misconceptions.message: The force is her weight = mass × g = 55 × 10 = 550 N, not 55. Pressure = 550 ÷ 0.0002 = 2 750 000 Pa. Using 55 gives 275 000.

guided_steps.say: Pressure = force ÷ area. The force is her weight = mass × g.

guided_steps.hint: Mass times gravity.
Dividing by 0.0002 is the same as multiplying by 5000.

guided_steps.done: Back to the 550 N force, so 2 750 000 Pa is right.
guided_steps.hint: Pressure times area returns the force.

gold.hint: To go from m/s to km/h, multiply by 3.6.

misconceptions.message: m/s to km/h multiplies by 3.6: 15 × 3.6 = 54 km/h. Dividing by 3.6 gives about 4.17, which is slower, the wrong way round.

guided_steps.say: m/s to km/h: multiply by 3.6 (each 1 m/s is 3.6 km/h).

guided_steps.hint: It is the number given in the question.

guided_steps.done: Back to 15 m/s, so 54 km/h is right.
guided_steps.hint: Dividing by 3.6 undoes the multiply.

problem_bank.gold_description: Two steps: find a hidden volume, total, or force before the compound measure.

bronze.title: Bronze: one formula, one step
steps: Pick the formula: speed = distance ÷ time, density = mass ÷ volume, pressure = force ÷ area.
Put the two numbers you are given into it.
Divide for the bottom of the triangle, multiply for the top, then write the units.

example.question: A car travels 240 km in 4 hours. Find the speed.

silver.title: Silver: rearrange or convert first
steps: Cover the quantity you want in the triangle to see whether to multiply or divide.
Convert units first if they do not match: km/h to m/s divide by 3.6, minutes to hours divide by 60.
Then apply the formula in one step and add the units.

gold.title: Gold: two steps before the measure
steps: Find the hidden quantity first: a volume from the solid, a total distance and total time, or a force from weight = mass × g.
For average speed use total distance ÷ total time, never the average of the two speeds.
Then apply the compound-measure formula and keep the units.

example.question: A cube of side 4 cm has mass 384 g. Find the density.

opener.label: Before any formula
opener.display: A car drives 120 miles in 2 hours, going the same speed the whole way.

steps.say: No formula needed, just common sense. Same speed each hour.
steps.hint: Split 120 miles fairly across the 2 hours.

steps.say: That number per hour IS the speed. You just did speed = distance ÷ time.
steps.pre: So in 3 hours it would go 60 × 3 =

steps.say: Those two moves are the whole lesson. Every quantity lives in a triangle: speed (distance, speed, time), density (mass, density, volume) and pressure (force, pressure, area). Cover the one you want: it tells you to multiply or divide.

steps.say: Now distance = speed × time, the top of the triangle.

silver.label: Rearrange the triangle
silver.display: <svg viewBox="0 0 200 160" role="img" aria-label="Formula triangle: force on top, pressure and area below" style="max-width:150px;display:block;margin:0 auto 8px"><polygon points="100,12 22,150 178,150" fill="#60a5fa" fill-opacity="0.15" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="53" y1="95" x2="147" y2="95" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="100" y1="95" x2="100" y2="150" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="100" y="70" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-family="Inter,sans-serif" font-size="26">F</text><text x="74" y="132" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-family="Inter,sans-serif" font-size="22">P</text><text x="126" y="132" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" font-family="Inter,sans-serif" font-size="22">A</text></svg>A press pushes with 250 Pa on an area of 0.4 m². Find the force. Then find the area that 500 N would cover at the same pressure.

steps.say: Force is the top: F = pressure × area.
For area, cover A: A = force ÷ pressure.

steps.done: Back to the 500 N force. It fits.

gold.label: Two steps before the measure
gold.display: A van drives 120 km at 40 km/h, then 120 km at 60 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole trip.

steps.say: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Find each time first.

steps.done: Not 50. The slow leg takes longer, so the average is pulled down.
